newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe bourse bull run continues unabated.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe bourse bull run continues unabated.

text.p: Zimbabwe's equity market soared to fresh highs on Thursday, rising 3.6 percent on aggressive local buying amid continued buoyant sentiment.
The 57-share industrial index leapt 339.24 points -- its largest gain ever on a single day -- to crash through the 9,500 psychological barrier, ending at a new all time high of 9,631.12.
"This thing seems to be chugging along and there's no stopping it. Everyone is very confident about everything," one broker said.

"Interest rates on the money market are down, inflation prospects for the year are looking good and there's also the rains which are probably the single most important factor which has boosted sentiment," he said.
Zimbabwe's farm-led economy is expected to grow by seven percent this year, up from an estimated five percent in 1996, on the back of good rains.

Leading Thursday's winners on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange, blue-chip beverages and supermarkets conglomerate Delta surged 300 cents in reasonable turnover to 4,300, hotel and supermarket group Meikles leapt 200 cents to 2,200 also in reasonable turnover, while clothing retailer Edgars jumped 150 cents to 4,350.

Horticultural group Ariston and bankers Barclays each rose 100 cents to 2,500 and 3,000 respectively, clothing retailer Truworths gained 60 cents to 1,310 while finance group Finhold at 900, sugar producer Hippo at 1,200 and tyre re-processor NTS at 550all added 50 cents.

Also among the winners, electronics group Apex put on 30 cents to 250 as did Caps to 380, cement producer Porthold and clothing and furniture retailer Tedco added 25 cents each to 1,475 and 1,275 respectively, bankers FMB rose 20 cents to 4,520 while a handful of other counters traded 15 cents higher.
Cement producer Circle was the day's only loser, shedding 10 cents to 850.

In minings, Falgold shrugged off a fall in the gold price on international price to trade five cents up at 95 but gold cunter Ashanti succumbed, dropping 2,000 cents to 8,000. Elsewhere on the mining board, Wankie Colliery lost 10 cents to 620 while nickel producer Bindura rose 40 cents to 900.
The seven-counter mining index gained 18.23 points to 1,153.42.
